name: trading-chart-debugging
description: Diagnose "the structure is right but the visuals are wrong" rendering bugs in trading dashboards — blank chart canvases, page sections that render unstyled, content hidden behind fixed-position background layers, pop-ups that appear shifted because animation overrides a CSS transform, and charts that render but show stale or wrong data. A class-level umbrella for the family of bugs where the build is clean, the DOM is correct, and computed styles prove your CSS rules are live while the page still looks broken. Covers the root causes that hit any Next.js App Router page or component with co-located CSS: a missing CSS import on the page or component (the build ships the React markup but never bundles the stylesheet), flexbox parents collapsing to their content's height (a chart, a scrollable panel, or any flex-column leaf that needs `min-height: 0`), fixed-position background layers painting over static-positioned sections (z-index has no effect on static elements), canvas libraries capturing `clientWidth`/`clientHeight` at mount before flexbox has measured, Framer Motion's `animate={{ x: 0 }}` clobbering a CSS `transform: translateX(-50%)` centering rule, lightweight-charts v5 typing and the `series.update()` full-OHLC requirement, period-rollover detection for live ticks, and stale "Cached" badges that don't track the underlying TTL. Use when a chart shows nothing but the watermark, when data flows but no shapes draw, when a page section renders as raw browser defaults despite a sibling CSS file existing, when `elementFromPoint` returns a background layer over your content, when `position: absolute` doesn't apply because the stylesheet isn't loaded, when a flex leaf collapses to its tallest child's height, when the last candle is frozen while the price ticker moves, or when any Next.js render looks "wrong but the build is clean.
